exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery)
cohort: The study included 23,359 hospitalized pregnant patients with heart failure or pulmonary hypertension who were primarily admitted for vaginal or cesarean delivery between 2011 and 2019, identified using the Nationwide Readmission Database.
finding: In pregnant patients with heart failure or pulmonary hypertension, cesarean delivery was associated with lower fetal mortality but higher in-hospital maternal mortality compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Compared to vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery was associated with lower odds of fetal mortality (OR: 0.18) but higher odds of in-hospital maternal mortality (OR: 2.0).
